correctness.rationale: The exact point-hyperplane distance matrix decomposes into one point-versus-hyperplane contrast and two transversal singular sectors of multiplicity v-1 each. The incidence identity N N^T=(k-lambda)I+lambda J gives the entire spectrum and normalization, not merely an empirical test. A monotonic ratio fixes the unique transversal root; q>=3 is settled by a strict logarithmic comparison. Small binary dimensions have exact rational root enclosures, dimensions 5-7 exact rational-power witnesses, and all d>=8 a uniform elementary Taylor bound. Li and Weston Theorem 5.4 rules out reentrant negative-type exponents. Finite incidence-and-spectrum reconstruction and exact interval tests pass in check.py. Endpoint nullities follow from strict separation of sectors. No unsupported infinite assertion rests on finite enumeration.

value.rationale: All-bandwidth positive definiteness is a natural Gaussian embedding invariant of the finite shortest-path metric, not a random matrix slice. The finite projective-space family is canonical and infinite in both dimension and field size. The exact binary dimension-five mode switch, the endpoint nullity jump from v-1 to one, and distinct 2^{-d} versus 2^{-d/2} obstructions explain a structural phase boundary not apparent from raw distance-spectrum listings. This exact classification has immediate implications for feasible Euclidean embeddings and universal-kernel choices on incidence data. The claim does not require a downstream theorem to be mathematically motivated.
